title: sdk migration lint + changelog extractor for v1->v2 ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight migration lint tool and automated changelog extractor that scans merged SDK PRs and code diffs to produce: (1) per-language migration hints for Python/TypeScript/Go (examples for retries, streaming ergonomics, and new structured-output APIs), (2) a machine-readable changelog delta used to populate the docs migration guide and release notes, and (3) suggested codemod transformations for common breaking changes. The tool will help solutions teams and customers accelerate v1->v2 migration by surfacing concrete code edits, sample snippets, and risk assessments (e.g., retry semantics changed from client-side automatic retires to explicit retry-policies).
acceptance_criteria: Tool runs in CI on merge and produces a JSON changelog delta summarizing API additions, deprecations, and behavioral changes
Generated migration guide contains language-specific examples for: retry behavior, streaming iterator -> async generator ergonomics, and embedding/structured-output signature changes
Codemod suggestions for the top 10 common breaking patterns (Python/TS/Go) are produced and verified against a sample repo
Docs repo receives an autogenerated draft migration page via a PR with the extracted changelog, and a human reviewer can accept or edit
End-to-end test that runs existing SDK example suite against suggested codemods to validate compilation/typing for TS/Go and runtime smoke tests for Python
updates: 2026-02-20: Scoped initial spike. Identified top recurring breaking patterns from last 6 months of SDK work: retry API rename, streaming response iterator changes, structured output/ function-calling payload shape updates.

2026-02-24: Prototype extractor that parses GitHub PR titles and diff hunks; produced first draft JSON delta for 10 merged PRs. Stored output in s3://redwood-internal/sdk-migration/deltas/2026-02-24.json.

2026-03-01: PoC codemod for Python using lib2to3-style AST transform; handles rename of `client.retry` -> `client.with_retry(policy=...)` and streaming `for chunk in resp:` -> `async for chunk in resp.stream()` with fallback shim insertion. Ran against internal examples repo: 14/18 fixes applied cleanly.

2026-03-05: Design review with DX (Marta Kim) and PM (Ravi Shah). Key decision: prefer 'suggested PR' workflow over auto-apply codemods for major behavioral changes. Added flag for experimental auto-apply in advanced migration mode.
2026-03-09: Implemented changelog template and docs PR generator. Test PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4120 (draft).
2026-03-12: Codeowner review requested. Awaiting feedback from runtime and SDK leads. Noted edge cases for Go generics-based client wrappers where codemod must be conservative.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive codemod vs conservative suggestions. We decided to err on conservative for Go and TypeScript public surface to avoid breaking typed consumers. For Python, we offer opt-in auto-apply for low-risk rewrites. The extractor will tag changes with risk scores (low/medium/high) based on test coverage heuristics and pattern complexity.
next_steps: Finish codeowner reviews and address runtime edge cases (KV cache/streaming buffer semantics)
Add TypeScript codemod using ts-morph and verify against @redwood/samples
Wire CI to open draft docs PR on release branch merges and notify docs-owner channel
Add an opt-in 'migration-run' job for customers using our Migration Console to preview suggested codemod changes against a forked repo
